title: Label every input
summary: Give every form control a visible label.
paragraphs: A placeholder disappears as soon as someone types. Use a label that stays on the page and describes the value you expect.
Match the label htmlFor to the input id. This connects the name for assistive technology and makes the label clickable.
When validation fails, explain the correction in text next to the field. Do not depend on a red border alone.

title: Keep state small
summary: Store user choices and derive the rest.
paragraphs: A filtered list can usually be calculated from the original list and the current query. Keeping another copy in state introduces a second value to synchronize.
Calculate inexpensive derived values during rendering. Add memoization only after measuring a real cost.
Place state near the component that needs it. Moving everything to a shared provider makes simple interactions harder to trace.

title: Render text safely
summary: Treat user input as text rather than markup.
paragraphs: For a plain DOM page, assign user content with textContent. It displays characters without interpreting them as HTML.
React escapes ordinary string children. Keep notes as strings and render paragraphs instead of assembling markup from input.
When formatted HTML is a requirement, choose a reviewed sanitization approach. Escaping text and sanitizing HTML solve different problems.

title: Start with one column
summary: Let content decide when the layout needs room.
paragraphs: A narrow layout is a useful starting point. Put the most important information first and keep the reading order meaningful.
Use a grid with a single column by default, then add a wider-screen breakpoint when cards have enough space.
Test long titles and keyboard focus at a narrow width. A tidy screenshot with short sample text does not prove the layout can handle real content.

title: Write useful errors
summary: Explain what happened and what can be done.
paragraphs: A useful validation message names the problem and the next action. “Enter a whole number from 1 to 99” is more helpful than “Invalid input.”
Preserve the values someone has already entered when possible. Losing their work makes a recoverable error more expensive.
A failed network request is different from an invalid field. Keep those states separate so the user does not change correct information.

title: Choose stable list keys
summary: Use identity rather than position for changing lists.
paragraphs: When a list can be reordered or filtered, the array index does not describe an item’s identity. Use a stable identifier from the data.
A key only needs to be unique among its siblings. A short permanent slug works well for a small authored collection.
Do not generate a random key during rendering. A changing key can cause components to remount and lose local state.
